'''''Petrea volubilis''''', commonly known as '''purple wreath''', '''queen's wreath''' or '''sandpaper vine''', is an evergreen flowering vine in the family [[Verbenaceae]], native to tropical America, that is valued especially for its display of violet flowers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Petrea volubilis L. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:330591-2|access-date=2020-08-26|publisher=Plants of the World Online|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Description ==
[[File:Petrea_volubillis_1.JPG|thumb]]
As a climbing plant, it grows to a height of {{cvt|12|m|ft|abbr=on}}, but as a shrub it grows to {{cvt|4|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall.<ref>[http://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Petrea+volubilis Petrea volubilis L. Verbenaceae] Tropical Plants Database, Ken Fern. tropical.theferns.info. 2021-02-04.</ref> It is a [[vine]] or semi-climbing shrub with [[Wikt:puberulent|puberulent]] stems, sometimes reaching {{cvt|10|cm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter. Leaves are elliptical-oblong, 5–16cm long and 3–8cm wide, apex [[glossary of leaf morphology|acute]] or obtuse, base wedge-shaped, entire margin, sometimes sinuous, glabrous or pubescent, rough to the touch; [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] 0.2–1 cm long.<ref>Correa A., M. D., C. Galdames & M. N. S. Stapf. 2004. Cat. Pl. Vasc. Panamá 1–599. Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, Panama.</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.flowersofindia.net/catalog/slides/Purple%20Wreath.html|title=''Petrea volubilis'' - Purple Wreath|publisher=www.flowersofindia.net|access-date=2019-04-12}}</ref>

The flowers emerge from bracts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://botanyphoto.botanicalgarden.ubc.ca/2014/03/petrea-volubilis/ |title=Petrea volubilis |website=botanyphoto.botanicalgarden.ubc.ca |date= 6 March 2014|access-date=2020-09-19}}</ref> [[Racemose]] inflorescences 8–20 cm long, axillary or terminal, solitary, puberulent [[rachis]], 5-mere flowers on puberulent [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]s supported by a [[deciduous]] bract ; calyx tube 0.2–0.7 cm long, glabrous or puberulent, [[Petal|corolla]] infundibuliform, 1 cm long, puberulent, blue; [[ovary]] and glabrous style. Drupaceous fruit completely enclosed in the acrid [[calyx (botany)|calyx]] which acts as wings or floats.

==Distribution and habitat == 
It is found especially on the banks of rivers and streams, from northern [[Mexico]] to [[Bolivia]], [[Brazil]] and [[Paraguay]] in the [[Antilles]] and in [[Venezuela]]. Depending on the climate, it can have up to two blooms in the year. Its very nectar-bearing flowers attract butterflies.<ref>Funk, V. A., P. E. Berry, S. Alexander, T. H. Hollowell & C. L. Kelloff. 2007. Checklist of the Plants of the Guiana Shield (Venezuela: Amazonas, Bolivar, Delta Amacuro; Guyana, Surinam, French Guiana). Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 55: 1–584.</ref>

==Cultivation==
In temperate climates, ''Petrea volubilis'' prefers full sun and can tolerate shade, although it will not flower profusely. It handles a very light and fleeting frost at temperatures down to -2 °C, but beyond this threshold the plant would die. It thrives in well drained, fertile soils and can tolerate [[drought]].<ref>[https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/39815 Petrea volubilis (queen's wreath)] by Jeanine Vélez-Gavilán, University of Puerto Rico at Mayagüez, Puerto Rico from [[Centre for Agriculture and Bioscience International]], 30 September 2019</ref>

The [[Wayapi]] ethnic group traditionally uses a preparation with sap to treat burns, wounds, inflammation and [[abscess]]es, and in the [[Caribbean]] it is used to treat [[diarrhea]].<ref>[http://nature.jardin.free.fr/1102/nmauric_petrea_volubilis.html Petrea volubilis - Pétrée volubile, Liane Saint Jean] by Jardin L'Encyclopédie</ref>
